stem: A hospital audits hand-hygiene opportunities and completed actions, then reports the results to staff. What is the primary purpose?

options.A: Use the results only to identify individual staff for discipline without unit-level improvement feedback.
options.B: Replace infection-prevention education with audit scores because measurement alone changes practice.
options.C: Use the results to identify adherence gaps and provide regular feedback that supports improvement.
options.D: Collect compliance data for reporting purposes without discussing findings or changing practice.

rationale: CDC Core Infection Prevention and Control Practices identify performance monitoring and feedback as a core practice: facilities should monitor adherence to infection-prevention practices, provide prompt and regular feedback on adherence and related outcomes to healthcare personnel and leadership, and act on surveillance data. Therefore C is correct. A limits monitoring to punishment rather than improvement, B incorrectly substitutes measurement for required education and training, and D disconnects collected data from feedback and corrective action.
educational_objective: Use infection-prevention audit data to identify adherence gaps, provide prompt and regular feedback, and support corrective improvement rather than treating measurement as an end in itself.
source_organization: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC)
source_document_title: CDC's Core Infection Prevention and Control Practices for Safe Healthcare Delivery in All Settings
source_locator: Core Practices Table > 4. Performance Monitoring and Feedback: identify and monitor adherence to infection-prevention practices and requirements; provide prompt, regular feedback on adherence and related outcomes to healthcare personnel and facility leadership; use standardized tools and definitions; monitor infection incidence and act on surveillance data. Core Practices Table > 2. Education and Training: provide job-specific education/training and additional training for recognized lapses.
source_claim_supported: Infection-prevention performance monitoring should identify adherence gaps, be paired with prompt and regular feedback, and inform improvement actions; it does not replace education or exist only for reporting or discipline.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
blueprint_locator: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control — implement and evaluate infection-prevention practices and safety measures that reduce transmission and protect clients and health care personnel.
blueprint_topic: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control — hand-hygiene adherence monitoring and feedback

source_original.stem: A hospital audits hand-hygiene opportunities and completed actions, then reports the results to staff. What is the primary purpose?

options.A: Use the results only to identify individual staff for discipline without unit-level improvement feedback.
options.B: Replace infection-prevention education with audit scores because measurement alone changes practice.
options.C: Use the results to identify adherence gaps and provide regular feedback that supports improvement.
options.D: Collect compliance data for reporting purposes without discussing findings or changing practice.

source_original.rationale: CDC recommends monitoring adherence to infection-prevention practices and providing prompt, regular feedback so gaps and outcomes can be improved. Option C is correct. Monitoring is not intended to replace education, function only as punishment, or remain disconnected from improvement.
source_original.source_detail: Performance Monitoring and Feedback: identify and monitor adherence to infection-prevention practices, use standardized tools when available, and provide prompt, regular feedback on adherence and related outcomes. Current CDC Core Practices live-rechecked 2026-08-15. NCSBN first-check: Client Needs — Safe and Effective Care Environment — Safety and Infection Prevention and Control: transmission precautions, PPE, device/environmental safety, asepsis, identification and infection-prevention activities as applicable. 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan; effective 2026-04-01 through 2029-03-31; currentness rechecked 2026-08-15.

correction_summary: Retained the original stem, options, and key C. Strengthened the rationale and exact CDC locator to include both feedback/action and the separate education/training requirement, preventing the item from implying that audit measurement alone changes practice.

audit_findings.source_authority: Current CDC Core Infection Prevention and Control Practices; NCSBN 2026 for blueprint
audit_findings.currentness: CDC page dated 2024-04-12 and live-rechecked 2026-08-16; CDC describes these core practices as fundamental standards not expected to change regularly
audit_findings.exact_locator: Core Practices Table > 4. Performance Monitoring and Feedback and > 2. Education and Training
audit_findings.claim_audit: Final item directly reflects CDC monitoring, regular feedback, action on data, and continued education/training. No unsupported compliance percentage, audit frequency, or disciplinary rule is added.

distractor_audit.A: Incorrectly makes discipline the sole use and omits improvement feedback.
distractor_audit.B: Incorrectly replaces required education/training with measurement alone.
distractor_audit.D: Incorrectly disconnects monitoring data from feedback and practice improvement.

audit_findings.ambiguity_second_answer: Only C combines adherence-gap identification with feedback and improvement, the functions supported by the CDC core practice.
audit_findings.cueing: All alternatives describe plausible organizational uses of audit data; no answer is distinguished by technical jargon or unsupported numbers.
audit_findings.blueprint: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control — monitoring and improving adherence to infection-prevention practices.
audit_findings.independent_second_pass: Rechecked the current CDC Core Practices table, each option, rationale, objective, NCSBN mapping, ambiguity and cueing from zero. C remained uniquely correct.
